business_meaning: Accuracy alone is misleading; ranking and PR metrics are required.

finding: Subscription prevalence changes sharply across chronological splits.
business_meaning: A static model is poorly calibrated across campaign periods; monitoring and retraining are mandatory.

finding: The selected histogram gradient boosting model is better than random but modest.
evidence: Test ROC-AUC 0.635; PR-AUC 0.513 vs test prevalence 0.385
business_meaning: Useful for prioritisation, not automatic rejection or approval.

finding: The top-scored 20% of test records contain 639 subscribers.
business_meaning: Ranking can concentrate likely responders when call capacity is limited.

finding: Validation-tuned threshold 0.101 balances precision and recall.
business_meaning: Threshold must be set from campaign economics, not F1 alone.

finding: Using call duration improves apparent scores but violates prediction timing.
business_meaning: A duration-based pre-call model would be invalid and misleading.

finding: A prior successful campaign is strongly associated with subscription.
business_meaning: Prior engagement is a useful ranking signal, but not proof of causal persistence.

finding: Cellular-contact records convert more often than telephone records.
business_meaning: Could reflect campaign period/client mix; channel experiments are needed.

finding: More current-campaign contacts are negatively associated with subscription.
business_meaning: Repeated contacts may signal hard-to-convert prospects or fatigue.

finding: Precision/recall and selection rates vary across age bands.
evidence: Recall ranges from 0.439 to 0.711; older bands have high selection/FPR
business_meaning: Human oversight and subgroup monitoring are needed to prevent unfair targeting.
